statement.text:
(J. Lauri). A card of a finite simple undirected graph G of order n = |V (G)|
is an induced subgraph of order n − 1. Let k be 2, 3, 4. For a connected graph G with
k isomorphism types of cards, can Aut(G) have more than k orbits on the vertex set
V (G)?
    If a graph G has k isomorphism types of cards, then the group Aut(G) of auto-
morphisms of G has obviously at least k orbits on V (G). It is known that if all cards
are mutually isomorphic, then Aut(G) is transitive on V (G). Examples are known of
graphs G with 5 isomorphism types of cards for which Aut(G) has 6 orbits on V (G),
and of graphs with 6 isomorphism types for which Aut(G) has 7 orbits on V (G).
                                                                               V. Pannone
